answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when independent audits confirm duplicate control or fabricated work. A garden of long-lived agents earns reputation gradually, while a tundra of freshly minted accounts must lock capital before gaining influence; splitting one operator across identities does not multiply that stake. The violet audit trail ties penalties to observable behavior, so an attacker pays both the capital cost and the risk of losing it.
